"""Claim families quote, scorecard, orders, forecast_cost_news, and signals(), on the 19 practice cases."""

import copy
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from hollerau.contracts import Claim
from hollerau.evidence.compile import compile_evidence
from hollerau.evidence.facts import check, facts_of, load_package
from hollerau.evidence.forecast_cost_news import forecast_cost_news_claims
from hollerau.evidence.orders import orders_claims
from hollerau.evidence.quote import quote_claims
from hollerau.evidence.scorecard import scorecard_claims
from hollerau.evidence.signals import signals

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
CASES = {c["case_id"]: c for c in json.loads((ROOT / "tests/fixtures/cases/practice.json").read_text())}


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def data():
    try:
        return load_package()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pytest.skip("no data package: run `uv run arena data` or set ARENA_DATA")


def run(family, case_id, data):
    case = CASES[case_id]
    facts = facts_of(case, data)
    claims = family(case, data, facts)
    for c in claims:
        assert check(c, facts), c
        assert all(i in c.sentence for i in c.ids), c
    return claims


@pytest.mark.parametrize("case_id", sorted(CASES))
def test_every_family_claim_is_verifiable(data, case_id):
    case = CASES[case_id]
    facts = facts_of(case, data)
    raw = [c for f in (quote_claims, scorecard_claims, orders_claims, forecast_cost_news_claims) for c in f(case, data, facts)]
    assert all(check(c, facts) for c in raw), [c for c in raw if not check(c, facts)]
    claims = compile_evidence(case, data)
    ids = [i for c in claims for i in c.ids]
    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids))


# --- quote


def test_rival_quote_above_the_stake_is_not_cited(data):
    """P01: the second source quotes 143.22 against 138.55 asked: it argues the supplier's case."""
    assert run(quote_claims, "case:P01", data) == []


def test_cheaper_rival_quote_is_cited(data):
    case = copy.deepcopy(CASES["case:P01"])
    case["refs"].append("quote:HIDDEN-1")
    case["facts"] = {"quote:HIDDEN-1": {"part": "part:310010", "supplier": "sup:70140", "unit_price": 131.0}}
    facts = facts_of(case, data)
    [c] = quote_claims(case, data, facts)
    assert c.ids == ["quote:HIDDEN-1"] and c.figure == 131.0 and c.unit == "EUR" and check(c, facts)


def test_quote_of_another_part_is_not_cited(data):
    case = copy.deepcopy(CASES["case:P01"])
    case["refs"].append("quote:HIDDEN-2")
    case["facts"] = {"quote:HIDDEN-2": {"part": "part:999999", "supplier": "sup:70140", "unit_price": 1.0}}
    assert quote_claims(case, data, facts_of(case, data)) == []


# --- scorecard


def test_p11_red_card_quality_first(data):
    claims = run(scorecard_claims, "case:P11", data)
    assert claims[0].ids == ["sc:70140@2026Q3"] and claims[0].unit == "ppm" and claims[0].figure == 2376
    assert claims[0].supports == "quality"


def test_p09_delivery_card(data):
    [c] = run(scorecard_claims, "case:P09", data)
    assert c.ids == ["sc:70220@2026Q3"] and c.unit == "%" and c.figure == 56.0


def test_green_card_is_not_cited(data):
    assert run(scorecard_claims, "case:P02", data) == []  # green, 273 ppm
    assert run(scorecard_claims, "case:P01", data) == []  # amber but 712 ppm and 85.2 % on time


def test_scorecard_check_uses_the_mean():
    facts = {"sc:1@Q1": {"ppm": 1000, "otd_pct": 80.0}, "sc:1@Q2": {"ppm": 2000, "otd_pct": 60.0}}
    claim = Claim("scorecard", ["sc:1@Q1", "sc:1@Q2"], 1500.0, "ppm", "", "quality")
    assert check(claim, facts)
    assert not check(Claim("scorecard", ["sc:1@Q1", "sc:1@Q2"], 2000.0, "ppm", "", "quality"), facts)
    assert check(Claim("scorecard", ["sc:1@Q1", "sc:1@Q2"], 70.0, "%", "", "other"), facts)


# --- orders


def test_p14_orders_show_the_price_already_rose(data):
    [c] = run(orders_claims, "case:P14", data)
    facts = facts_of(CASES["case:P14"], data)
    first, last = (facts[i] for i in c.ids)
    assert first["part"] == last["part"] == "part:350040"
    assert last["unit_price"] == 316.35 and last["unit_price"] > first["unit_price"] * 1.03
    assert c.figure is None and "per 100 pcs" in c.sentence


def test_orders_without_a_rise_are_not_cited(data):
    assert run(orders_claims, "case:P01", data) == []  # 128.27 -> 126.53: it fell


def test_orders_check_needs_one_part():
    facts = {"po:1": {"part": "part:1", "unit_price": 1.0}, "po:2": {"part": "part:2", "unit_price": 1.0}}
    assert not check(Claim("orders", ["po:1", "po:2"], None, "", "", "price"), facts)
    assert not check(Claim("orders", ["po:1"], None, "", "", "price"), {"po:1": facts["po:1"]})


# --- forecast_cost_news


def test_should_cost_cited_only_with_room(data):
    p06 = [c for c in run(forecast_cost_news_claims, "case:P06", data) if c.ids[0].startswith("cost:")]
    assert [c.ids for c in p06] == [["cost:310070"]] and p06[0].figure == 194.18
    for case_id in ("case:P01", "case:P02", "case:P03", "case:P14"):  # within the should-cost's 15 % error
        claims = run(forecast_cost_news_claims, case_id, data)
        assert not [c for c in claims if c.ids[0].startswith("cost:")], case_id


def test_forecast_growth_is_cited(data):
    [fc] = [c for c in run(forecast_cost_news_claims, "case:P01", data) if c.ids[0].startswith("fc:")]
    assert fc.ids == ["fc:310010@2026-09"] and fc.figure == 10.1 and fc.supports == "volume"


def test_news_only_when_it_weakens_the_supplier(data):
    p05 = [c for c in run(forecast_cost_news_claims, "case:P05", data) if c.ids[0].startswith("news:")]
    assert [c.ids for c in p05] == [["news:20260309-03"]]  # free capacity; not full_order_book (70240)
    p11 = run(forecast_cost_news_claims, "case:P11", data)
    assert not [c for c in p11 if c.ids[0].startswith("news:")]  # restructuring: not ours to cite


def test_fcn_check_rejects_a_wrong_figure():
    facts = {"fc:1@2026-09": {"change_pct": 10.0}, "cost:1": {"unit_cost": 100.0}, "news:1": {"supplier": "sup:1"}}
    assert check(Claim("forecast_cost_news", ["fc:1@2026-09"], 10.4, "%", "", "volume"), facts)
    assert not check(Claim("forecast_cost_news", ["fc:1@2026-09"], 11.0, "%", "", "volume"), facts)
    assert not check(Claim("forecast_cost_news", ["cost:1"], 101.0, "EUR", "", "price"), facts)
    assert not check(Claim("forecast_cost_news", ["news:1"], 1.0, "", "", "other"), facts)


# --- compile order


def test_p01_strongest_first(data):
    families = [c.family for c in compile_evidence(CASES["case:P01"], data)]
    assert families[0] == "notice" and families.index("index") < families.index("forecast_cost_news")


# --- signals


def test_signals_p02_increase_justified(data):
    s = signals(CASES["case:P02"], data)
    assert s["increase_justified"] is True and s["weighted_index_pct"]["part:350011"] > s["asked_pct"]
    assert signals(CASES["case:P01"], data)["increase_justified"] is False
    assert signals(CASES["case:P03"], data)["increase_justified"] is None  # no price letter


def test_signals_material_hedged(data):
    for case_id, sup in (("case:P08", "sup:70710"), ("case:P14", "sup:70560")):
        s = signals(CASES[case_id], data)["suppliers"][sup]
        assert s["material_hedged_until"] == "March 2027" and s["material_hedged"], case_id


def test_signals_p11_cash_need(data):
    s = signals(CASES["case:P11"], data)["suppliers"]["sup:70140"]
    assert "doc:20260715-70140-M1" in s["cash_need"]


def test_signals_committee_capacity_single_source_payments(data):
    p17 = signals(CASES["case:P17"], data)["suppliers"]["sup:70550"]
    assert p17["committee_above_pct"] == 2.0 and p17["single_source"] is True
    p01 = signals(CASES["case:P01"], data)["suppliers"]["sup:70110"]
    assert p01["single_source"] is False  # sup:70140 is qualified for part:310010
    assert signals(CASES["case:P19"], data)["suppliers"]["sup:70640"]["free_capacity"]
    pay = p01["our_late_payments"]
    assert pay["invoices"] > 0 and 0 <= pay["late_share"] <= 1


def test_signals_ignore_notes_after_the_letter(data):
    """Notes are read up to the case's letter date, never after it."""
    s = signals(CASES["case:P01"], data)["suppliers"]["sup:70110"]
    ids = [i for v in s.values() if isinstance(v, list) for i in v]
    assert all(i.split(":")[1][:8] <= "20260911" for i in ids if i.startswith("doc:"))

def test_orders_without_a_rise_are_not_cited(data):
    assert run(orders_claims, "case:P01", data) == []  # 128.27 -> 126.53: it fell


def test_orders_check_needs_one_part():
    facts = {"po:1": {"part": "part:1", "unit_price": 1.0}, "po:2": {"part": "part:2", "unit_price": 1.0}}
    assert not check(Claim("orders", ["po:1", "po:2"], None, "", "", "price"), facts)
    assert not check(Claim("orders", ["po:1"], None, "", "", "price"), {"po:1": facts["po:1"]})


# --- forecast_cost_news


def test_should_cost_cited_only_with_room(data):
    p06 = [c for c in run(forecast_cost_news_claims, "case:P06", data) if c.ids[0].startswith("cost:")]
    assert [c.ids for c in p06] == [["cost:310070"]] and p06[0].figure == 194.18
    for case_id in ("case:P01", "case:P02", "case:P03", "case:P14"):  # within the should-cost's 15 % error
        claims = run(forecast_cost_news_claims, case_id, data)
        assert not [c for c in claims if c.ids[0].startswith("cost:")], case_id


def test_forecast_growth_is_cited(data):
    [fc] = [c for c in run(forecast_cost_news_claims, "case:P01", data) if c.ids[0].startswith("fc:")]
    assert fc.ids == ["fc:310010@2026-09"] and fc.figure == 10.1 and fc.supports == "volume"

    p05 = [c for c in run(forecast_cost_news_claims, "case:P05", data) if c.ids[0].startswith("news:")]
    assert [c.ids for c in p05] == [["news:20260309-03"]]  # free capacity; not full_order_book (70240)
    p11 = run(forecast_cost_news_claims, "case:P11", data)
    assert not [c for c in p11 if c.ids[0].startswith("news:")]  # restructuring: not ours to cite


def test_fcn_check_rejects_a_wrong_figure():
    facts = {"fc:1@2026-09": {"change_pct": 10.0}, "cost:1": {"unit_cost": 100.0}, "news:1": {"supplier": "sup:1"}}
    assert check(Claim("forecast_cost_news", ["fc:1@2026-09"], 10.4, "%", "", "volume"), facts)
    assert not check(Claim("forecast_cost_news", ["fc:1@2026-09"], 11.0, "%", "", "volume"), facts)
    assert not check(Claim("forecast_cost_news", ["cost:1"], 101.0, "EUR", "", "price"), facts)
    assert not check(Claim("forecast_cost_news", ["news:1"], 1.0, "", "", "other"), facts)


# --- compile order


def test_p01_strongest_first(data):
    families = [c.family for c in compile_evidence(CASES["case:P01"], data)]
    assert families[0] == "notice" and families.index("index") < families.index("forecast_cost_news")


# --- signals


def test_signals_p02_increase_justified(data):
    s = signals(CASES["case:P02"], data)
    assert s["increase_justified"] is True and s["weighted_index_pct"]["part:350011"] > s["asked_pct"]
    assert signals(CASES["case:P01"], data)["increase_justified"] is False
    assert signals(CASES["case:P03"], data)["increase_justified"] is None  # no price letter


def test_signals_material_hedged(data):
    for case_id, sup in (("case:P08", "sup:70710"), ("case:P14", "sup:70560")):
        s = signals(CASES[case_id], data)["suppliers"][sup]
        assert s["material_hedged_until"] == "March 2027" and s["material_hedged"], case_id


def test_signals_p11_cash_need(data):
    s = signals(CASES["case:P11"], data)["suppliers"]["sup:70140"]
    assert "doc:20260715-70140-M1" in s["cash_need"]


def test_signals_committee_capacity_single_source_payments(data):
    p17 = signals(CASES["case:P17"], data)["suppliers"]["sup:70550"]
    assert p17["committee_above_pct"] == 2.0 and p17["single_source"] is True
    p01 = signals(CASES["case:P01"], data)["suppliers"]["sup:70110"]
    assert p01["single_source"] is False  # sup:70140 is qualified for part:310010
    assert signals(CASES["case:P19"], data)["suppliers"]["sup:70640"]["free_capacity"]
    pay = p01["our_late_payments"]
    assert pay["invoices"] > 0 and 0 <= pay["late_share"] <= 1


def test_signals_ignore_notes_after_the_letter(data):
    """Notes are read up to the case's letter date, never after it."""
    s = signals(CASES["case:P01"], data)["suppliers"]["sup:70110"]
    ids = [i for v in s.values() if isinstance(v, list) for i in v]
    assert all(i.split(":")[1][:8] <= "20260911" for i in ids if i.startswith("doc:"))

  ❌ <con>

D-numbering: first question in a skill invocation is `D1`; increment yourself. This is a model-level instruction, not a runtime counter.

ELI10 is always present, in plain English, not function names. Recommendation is ALWAYS present. Keep the `(recommended)` label; AUTO_DECIDE depends on it.

Completeness: use `Completeness: N/10` only when options differ in coverage. 10 = complete, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut. If options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.`

Accepted shortcuts leave a trail: when the user selects an option that is BOTH Completeness ≤ 7 AND a durable-scope call (architecture or scope-cut — never a turn-level choice), log it via `gstack-decision-log` with the ceiling and the upgrade trigger in the rationale, and — as part of implementing that option, same edit, no follow-up question — mark each cut corner in code with `gstack-shortcut(dec-<id>): <ceiling>, upgrade when <trigger>` in the language's comment syntax. Never agent-initiated: the marker exists only downstream of the user's explicit choice. /retro harvests these into a debt ledger, joined on the decision id.

`Pros / cons:` in question text; descriptions use literal ✅/❌ bullets, not Pro:/Con:. Each real option: ≥2 pros and ≥1 con, ≥40 chars each. One-way/destructive escape: `✅ No cons — this is a hard-stop choice`.

Neutral posture: `Recommendation: <default> — this is a taste call, no strong preference either way`; `(recommended)` STAYS on the default option for AUTO_DECIDE.

Effort both-scales: when an option involves effort, label both human-team and CC+gstack time, e.g. `(human: ~2 days / CC: ~15 min)`. Makes AI compression visible at decision time.

`Net:` line closes question text. Per-skill instructions may add stricter rules.

### Handling 5+ options — split, never drop

AskUserQuestion caps every call at **4 options**. With 5+ real options, NEVER
drop, merge, or silently defer one to fit: **batch into ≤4-groups** (coherent
alternatives) or **split per-option** (independent scope items — the default
when unsure): sequential `D<N>.k` calls, each with its ELI10, Recommendation,
kind-note, and buckets **A) Include, B) Defer, C) Cut, D) Hold** (stop chain,
discuss); a `D<N>.final` validates the assembled set; for N>6 fire a
`D<N>.0` meta-question first. Split question_ids: `<skill>-split-<option-slug>`
(kebab-case ASCII, ≤64 chars) — the runtime checker (`bin/gstack-question-preference`) refuses `never-ask` on
any `*-split-*` id, so split chains are never AUTO_DECIDE-eligible: the
user's option set is sacred.

**Full rule + worked examples + Hold/dependency semantics:**
`~/.claude/skills/gstack/docs/askuserquestion-split.md`. Read on demand when N>4.

**Non-ASCII characters — write directly, never \u-escape.** Emit literal
UTF-8 for Chinese (繁體/簡體), Japanese, Korean, or any non-ASCII text; never
`\uXXXX`-escape it (the pipe is UTF-8 native; manual escaping miscodes long
CJK strings). Only `\n`, `\t`, `\"`, `\\` remain allowed. Full rationale +
worked example: Read `~/.claude/skills/gstack/docs/askuserquestion-cjk.md`
on demand when a question contains CJK.

## Voice

GStack voice: Garry-shaped product and engineering judgment.

- Lead with the point. Say what it does, why it matters, and what changes for the builder.
- Be concrete. Name files, functions, line numbers, commands, outputs, evals, and real numbers.
- Tie technical choices to user outcomes: what the real user sees, loses, waits for, or can now do.
- Be direct about quality. Bugs matter. Edge cases matter. Fix the whole thing, not the demo path.
- Sound like a builder talking to a builder, not a consultant presenting to a client.
- Never corporate, academic, PR, or hype. Avoid filler, throat-clearing, generic optimism, and founder cosplay.
- No em dashes. No AI vocabulary: delve, crucial, robust, comprehensive, nuanced, multifaceted, furthermore, moreover, additionally, pivotal, landscape, tapestry, underscore, foster, showcase, intricate, vibrant, fundamental, significant, load-bearing.
- Reply in the language of the user's latest message unless asked otherwise. Code, commands, paths, identifiers, quoted output and question markers (`D<N>`, option letters, `(recommended)`) stay verbatim.
- The user has context you do not: domain knowledge, timing, relationships, taste. Cross-model agreement is a recommendation, not a decision. The user decides.

Good: "auth.ts:47 returns undefined when the session cookie expires. Users hit a white screen. Fix: add a null check and redirect to /login. Two lines."
Bad: "I've identified a potential issue in the authentication flow that may cause problems under certain conditions."

**Bounded closer.** After completing work, report in at most a few short lines: what changed, what was skipped, what to watch. No feature tours or unrequested design notes. Exempt: decision briefs, completion-status blocks, requested explanations, and a skill's mandated report (/qa-only, /plan-*-review, /retro, /document-generate). The rule limits prose around the deliverable, never the deliverable.

Good closer: "Renamed the flag in 3 files, regenerated docs, tests green. Skipped the CLI alias (unused since v1.2); watch the Windows job."
Bad closer: a tour of every edit, a restatement of the plan, and three paragraphs justifying choices nobody questioned.

## Completeness Principle — Boil the Ocean

AI makes completeness cheap, so the complete thing is the goal. Recommend full coverage (tests, edge cases, error paths) — boil the ocean one lake at a time. The only thing out of scope is genuinely unrelated work (rewrites, multi-quarter migrations); flag that as separate scope, never as an excuse for a shortcut.

When options differ in coverage, include `Completeness: X/10` (10 = all edge cases, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut). When options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.` Do not fabricate scores.

## Confusion Protocol

For high-stakes ambiguity (architecture, data model, destructive scope, missing context), STOP. Name it in one sentence, present 2-3 options with tradeoffs, and ask. Do not use for routine coding or obvious changes.

A claimed limitation or requirement ("the API can't do this", "X requires a credential", "that's impossible on this platform") is a material claim. State one only with the verbatim error, the documented statement, or a live probe in hand — pattern-matching a failure to a familiar story is not evidence. When a cheap probe settles the question, run it BEFORE asking the user anything or declaring a step blocked.

## Step 0: Detect platform and base branch

First, detect the git hosting platform from the remote URL:

```bash
git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null
```

- If the URL contains "github.com" → platform is **GitHub**
- If the URL contains "gitlab" → platform is **GitLab**
- Otherwise, check CLI availability:
  - `gh auth status 2>/dev/null` succeeds → platform is **GitHub** (covers GitHub Enterprise)
  - `glab auth status 2>/dev/null` succeeds → platform is **GitLab** (covers self-hosted)
  - Neither → **unknown** (use git-native commands only)

Determine which branch this PR/MR targets, or the repo's default branch if no
PR/MR exists. Use the result as "the base branch" in all subsequent steps.

**If GitHub:**
1. `gh pr view --json baseRefName -q .baseRefName` — if succeeds, use it
2. `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef -q .defaultBranchRef.name` — if succeeds, use it

**If GitLab:**
1. `glab mr view -F json 2>/dev/null` and extract the `target_branch` field — if succeeds, use it
2. `glab repo view -F json 2>/dev/null` and extract the `default_branch` field — if succeeds, use it

**Git-native fallback (if unknown platform, or CLI commands fail):**
1. `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null | sed 's|refs/remotes/origin/||'`
2. If that fails: `git rev-parse --verify origin/main 2>/dev/null` → use `main`
3. If that fails: `git rev-parse --verify origin/master 2>/dev/null` → use `master`

If all fail, fall back to `main`.

Print the detected base branch name. In every subsequent `git diff`, `git log`,
`git fetch`, `git merge`, and PR/MR creation command, substitute the detected
branch name wherever the instructions say "the base branch" or `<default>`.

### Shared-code opportunities (core pass)

Run this check on every diff, including fewer than 50 changed lines and hosts without Review Army:
1. Read the changed code and related unchanged callers using the rubric below. Do not run the standalone history/PR sweep or impose candidate quotas.
2. Require at least one verified authored location changed in this diff and at least two actual authored source locations needing the shared behavior. Added or uncommitted source qualifies; invented future callers do not.
3. Trace generated copies to authored templates/resolvers. Exclude generated and third-party copies from evidence and savings.

### Shared-code evaluation rubric

- **Prove the callers.** Require at least two verified, first-party authored source
  locations, with functions and lines. Actual added or uncommitted source qualifies.
  Only an engineering-plan review may use proposed callers; label those assumptions
  and distinguish them from existing source. Similar names or formatting alone do
  not establish equivalent behavior. Generated and third-party copies cannot qualify
  as callers or contribute savings. Follow generated copies back to authored
  templates/resolvers. Existing dependencies remain valid reuse targets.
- **Reuse before extracting.** Inspect existing libraries and helpers first. Compare
  behavior, inputs, outputs, error handling, side effects, security requirements,
  dependencies, and deployment/runtime boundaries. Preserve differences callers need;
  do not bridge languages or isolated deployments without a practical shared contract.
- **Keep the helper small.** Name its destination and contract, the callers to migrate,
  and the smallest adoption sequence. Avoid option-heavy helpers and coupling unrelated
  components. Point to existing tests or established use, specify shared-contract and
  caller-integration coverage, and describe the blast radius of a shared failure.
- **Account for the whole change.** Name removed blocks and their replacements. Show
  estimated implementation lines removed, added, and saved separately from total lines
  removed, added, and saved including tests and integration. Savings = removed - added.
  Count moved code on both sides, exclude generated/vendor lines, use ranges when
  uncertain, and do not count overlapping removals twice across opportunities. State
  when tests or integration may make the total change grow.
- **Rank useful changes.** Favor reliability gains and total net savings, then low
  adoption and testing risk. Prefer proven code used by several callers. Use recent
  activity to break ties between comparable benefits, not as evidence by itself.
  Explain choices centered on older code. Reject similarities with incompatible
  contracts and opportunities whose benefits do not justify the abstraction.

## Confidence Calibration

Verify evidence first, then score every finding (1-10) and apply its display rule.

### Pre-emit verification gate

1. **Quote the specific code line:** file:line and verbatim text. For a missing field,
   quote its class definition; for a nullable value, its initialization; for a race, both sides.
2. For framework-generated symbols, read and quote their generating metaclass,
   descriptor, ORM Meta block, migration, decorator or schema. Missing literal
   names in the class body or grep results do not prove absence.
3. **If you cannot quote the motivating line(s), the finding is unverified.**
   Force its confidence to 4-5: use 4 for appendix-only reporting, or 5 only when
   the finding belongs in the main report with the medium-confidence caveat below.
   Never invent speculative confidence 7+.

| Score | Meaning | Display rule |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| 9-10 | Specific code verifies a concrete bug or exploit. | Show normally |
| 7-8 | High-confidence pattern match; very likely correct. | Show normally |
| 5-6 | Moderate; could be a false positive. | Show with caveat: "Medium confidence, verify this is actually an issue" |
| 3-4 | Suspicious but may be fine. | Suppress from main report. Include in appendix only. |
| 1-2 | Speculation. | Only report a suspected release-blocking catastrophe (widespread data loss, total outage or system-wide compromise); label it CRITICAL and explicitly speculative. |

**Finding format:**

`[CRITICAL|INFORMATIONAL] (confidence: N/10) file:line — description`

Example:
`[CRITICAL] (confidence: 9/10) user.rb:42 — SQL injection via string interpolation`

**Calibration learning:** If the user confirms a reported finding scored < 7 is
real, log the corrected pattern as a learning.

### TODOS cross-reference

Flag new TODOs as informational and cite related items. Otherwise skip silently.

but its doc was not updated, flag an INFORMATIONAL finding naming the file and
affected behavior. Propose `/document-release` for the parent's decision, never a
critical finding or another writer during collection. Skip silently if no docs exist.

# Pre-Landing Review Checklist

## Instructions

Review the merge-base diff from the caller, including its selected uncommitted and new source. Use the caller's detected base, not a hardcoded branch. Cite `file:line` and suggest fixes. Only flag real problems.

**Two-pass review:**
- **Pass 1 (CRITICAL):** Run SQL & Data Safety, Race Conditions, LLM Output Trust Boundary, Shell Injection, and Enum Completeness first. Highest severity.
- **Pass 2 (INFORMATIONAL):** Run remaining categories below. Lower severity but still actioned.
- **Specialist categories (handled by parallel subagents, NOT this checklist):** Test Gaps, Dead Code, Magic Numbers, Conditional Side Effects, Performance & Bundle Impact, Crypto & Entropy, Simplification (unrequested structure). See `review/specialists/` for these.

Completeness Gaps and Simplification are orthogonal, not contradictory: Completeness pushes coverage UP (tests, edge cases, error paths), Simplification pushes unrequested structure DOWN (one-implementation abstractions, hand-rolled stdlib, dead flexibility). The same diff can legitimately receive both.

All findings get action via Fix-First Review: obvious mechanical fixes are applied automatically,
genuinely ambiguous issues are batched into a single user question.

**Output format:**

```
Pre-Landing Review: N issues (X critical, Y informational)

**AUTO-FIXED:**
- [file:line] Problem → fix applied

**NEEDS INPUT:**
- [file:line] Problem description
  Recommended fix: suggested fix
```

If no issues found: `Pre-Landing Review: No issues found.`

Be terse. For each issue: one line describing the problem, one line with the fix. No preamble, no summaries, no "looks good overall."

---

## Review Categories

### Pass 1 — CRITICAL

#### SQL & Data Safety
- String interpolation in SQL (even if values are `.to_i`/`.to_f` — use parameterized queries (Rails: sanitize_sql_array/Arel; Node: prepared statements; Python: parameterized queries))
- TOCTOU races: check-then-set patterns that should be atomic `WHERE` + `update_all`
- Bypassing model validations for direct DB writes (Rails: update_column; Django: QuerySet.update(); Prisma: raw queries)
- N+1 queries: Missing eager loading (Rails: .includes(); SQLAlchemy: joinedload(); Prisma: include) for associations used in loops/views

#### Race Conditions & Concurrency
- Read-check-write without uniqueness constraint or catch duplicate key error and retry (e.g., `where(hash:).first` then `save!` without handling concurrent insert)
- find-or-create without unique DB index — concurrent calls can create duplicates
- Status transitions that don't use atomic `WHERE old_status = ? UPDATE SET new_status` — concurrent updates can skip or double-apply transitions
- Unsafe HTML rendering (Rails: .html_safe/raw(); React: dangerouslySetInnerHTML; Vue: v-html; Django: |safe/mark_safe) on user-controlled data (XSS)

#### LLM Output Trust Boundary
- LLM-generated values (emails, URLs, names) written to DB or passed to mailers without format validation. Add lightweight guards (`EMAIL_REGEXP`, `URI.parse`, `.strip`) before persisting.
- Structured tool output (arrays, hashes) accepted without type/shape checks before database writes.
- LLM-generated URLs fetched without allowlist — SSRF risk if URL points to internal network (Python: `urllib.parse.urlparse` → check hostname against blocklist before `requests.get`/`httpx.get`)
- LLM output stored in knowledge bases or vector DBs without sanitization — stored prompt injection risk

#### Shell Injection (Python-specific)
- `subprocess.run()` / `subprocess.call()` / `subprocess.Popen()` with `shell=True` AND f-string/`.format()` interpolation in the command string — use argument arrays instead
- `os.system()` with variable interpolation — replace with `subprocess.run()` using argument arrays
- `eval()` / `exec()` on LLM-generated code without sandboxing

#### Enum & Value Completeness
When the diff introduces a new enum value, status string, tier name, or type constant, or loosens what an input accepts (a new MIME type, extension or flag, or a widened validator/parser/guard):
- **Trace it through every consumer.** Read (don't just grep — READ) each file that switches on, filters by, or displays that value. If any consumer doesn't handle the new value, flag it. Common miss: adding a value to the frontend dropdown but the backend model/compute method doesn't persist it.
- **Check allowlists/filter arrays.** Search for arrays or `%w[]` lists containing sibling values (e.g., if adding "revise" to tiers, find every `%w[quick lfg mega]` and verify "revise" is included where needed).
- **Check `case`/`if-elsif` chains.** If existing code branches on the enum, does the new value fall through to a wrong default?
- **Loosened acceptance breaks unchanged consumers.** Grep every consumer of the same field and confirm each handles the newly accepted shape; the broken code is usually outside the diff.
To do this: use Grep to find all references to the sibling values (e.g., grep for "lfg" or "mega" to find all tier consumers). Read each match. This step requires reading code OUTSIDE the diff.

### Pass 2 — INFORMATIONAL

#### Async/Sync Mixing (Python-specific)
- Synchronous `subprocess.run()`, `open()`, `requests.get()` inside `async def` endpoints — blocks the event loop. Use `asyncio.to_thread()`, `aiofiles`, or `httpx.AsyncClient` instead.
- `time.sleep()` inside async functions — use `asyncio.sleep()`
- Sync DB calls in async context without `run_in_executor()` wrapping

#### Column/Field Name Safety
- Verify column names in ORM queries (`.select()`, `.eq()`, `.gte()`, `.order()`) against actual DB schema — wrong column names silently return empty results or throw swallowed errors
- Check `.get()` calls on query results use the column name that was actually selected
- Cross-reference with schema documentation when available

#### Dead Code & Consistency (version/changelog only — other items handled by maintainability specialist)
- Version mismatch between PR title and VERSION/CHANGELOG files
- CHANGELOG entries that describe changes inaccurately (e.g., "changed from X to Y" when X never existed)

#### LLM Prompt Issues
- 0-indexed lists in prompts (LLMs reliably return 1-indexed)
- Prompt text listing available tools/capabilities that don't match what's actually wired up in the `tool_classes`/`tools` array
- Word/token limits stated in multiple places that could drift

#### Completeness Gaps
- Shortcut implementations where the complete version would cost <30 minutes CC time (e.g., partial enum handling, incomplete error paths, missing edge cases that are straightforward to add)
- Options presented with only human-team effort estimates — should show both human and CC+gstack time
- Test coverage gaps where adding the missing tests is a "lake" not an "ocean" (e.g., missing negative-path tests, missing edge case tests that mirror happy-path structure)
- Features implemented at 80-90% when 100% is achievable with modest additional code

#### Time Window Safety
- Date-key lookups that assume "today" covers 24h — report at 8am PT only sees midnight→8am under today's key
- Mismatched time windows between related features — one uses hourly buckets, another uses daily keys for the same data

#### Type Coercion at Boundaries
- Values crossing Ruby→JSON→JS boundaries where type could change (numeric vs string) — hash/digest inputs must normalize types
- Hash/digest inputs that don't call `.to_s` or equivalent before serialization — `{ cores: 8 }` vs `{ cores: "8" }` produce different hashes

#### View/Frontend
- Inline `<style>` blocks in partials (re-parsed every render)
- O(n*m) lookups in views (`Array#find` in a loop instead of `index_by` hash)
- Ruby-side `.select{}` filtering on DB results that could be a `WHERE` clause (unless intentionally avoiding leading-wildcard `LIKE`)

#### Distribution & CI/CD Pipeline
- CI/CD workflow changes (`.github/workflows/`): verify build tool versions match project requirements, artifact names/paths are correct, secrets use `${{ secrets.X }}` not hardcoded values
- New artifact types (CLI binary, library, package): verify a publish/release workflow exists and targets correct platforms
- Cross-platform builds: verify CI matrix covers all target OS/arch combinations, or documents which are untested
- Version tag format consistency: `v1.2.3` vs `1.2.3` — must match across VERSION file, git tags, and publish scripts
- Publish step idempotency: re-running the publish workflow should not fail (e.g., `gh release delete` before `gh release create`)

**DO NOT flag:**
- Web services with existing auto-deploy pipelines (Docker build + K8s deploy)
- Internal tools not distributed outside the team
- Test-only CI changes (adding test steps, not publish steps)

---

## Severity Classification

```
CRITICAL (highest severity):      INFORMATIONAL (main agent):      SPECIALIST (parallel subagents):
├─ SQL & Data Safety              ├─ Async/Sync Mixing             ├─ Testing specialist
├─ Race Conditions & Concurrency  ├─ Column/Field Name Safety      ├─ Maintainability specialist
├─ LLM Output Trust Boundary      ├─ Dead Code (version only)      ├─ Security specialist
├─ Shell Injection                ├─ LLM Prompt Issues             ├─ Performance specialist
└─ Enum & Value Completeness      ├─ Completeness Gaps             ├─ Data Migration specialist
                                   ├─ Time Window Safety            ├─ API Contract specialist
                                   ├─ Type Coercion at Boundaries   ├─ Simplification (advisory)
                                   ├─ View/Frontend                 └─ Red Team (conditional)
                                   └─ Distribution & CI/CD Pipeline

All findings are actioned via Fix-First Review. Severity determines
presentation order and classification of AUTO-FIX vs ASK — critical
findings lean toward ASK (they're riskier), informational findings
lean toward AUTO-FIX (they're more mechanical).
```

---

## Fix-First Heuristic

This heuristic is referenced by both `/review` and `/ship`. It determines whether
the agent auto-fixes a finding or asks the user.

- Shortcut implementations where the complete version would cost <30 minutes CC time (e.g., partial enum handling, incomplete error paths, missing edge cases that are straightforward to add)

- Date-key lookups that assume "today" covers 24h — report at 8am PT only sees midnight→8am under today's key

- Values crossing Ruby→JSON→JS boundaries where type could change (numeric vs string) — hash/digest inputs must normalize types

<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>I found 15 problems in `hollerau/evidence/`. Two crash `compile_case` on plausible hidden cases, three lose value without any error, and the rest are claim-quality or robustness issues. I edited no repo file, ran no git command that changes state, and used no network.

**What I ran.** The test suite passes (117 tests). I ran `compile_evidence`, `compile_case` and `signals` over all 19 practice cases, then 13 modified P01, P05 and P14 cases. Last, I loaded a fake Sunday release (under `/private/tmp/claude-501/rev/`) to see whether `signals` reads its documents. The probe scripts are `p1.py`, `p2.py` and `p3.py` in that folder.

**Tests (summary only).** The three test files check the code against its own `facts.check`, not against the arena. They cover the 19 practice cases, one positive and one negative test per claim family, D1/D2/D3, the P01 cost cross-check against the recorded session, one hidden case with its own `facts`, and the Sunday release extending an index window. Nothing tests:
- a must-have on the price, or on a field that only the supplier's quote fills
- a negotiable field with no options when the quote's standard terms are known
- Sunday news or letters dated after the case's letter
- price units that differ between a case and a quote
- fields set to null
- a bundle with should-cost or quote rows

## Crashes

1. **`economics.py:95-99` and `:63-68`, plus the `ValueError` at `:64`/`:68`.** `ok()` checks the must-haves with the price fixed at the asked price, and before the supplier's quote is read.
   - I ran: P01 with the must-have `unit_price <= 130` raises "no combination of term_options meets the must-haves".
   - I ran: P01 with `ppm_commitment <= 1000` when that field is neither negotiable nor fixed raises the same error. Before round 0 the field is None, and the kit treats None with `<=` as a failure.
   - Either one stops the whole case in a hidden final case.
   - FIXABLE: leave out `unit_price`, and fields that are neither in the grid nor in the closing terms, when checking must-haves for the grid search. Never raise; log and return the cheapest combination instead.

2. **`forecast_cost_news.py:76` and `signals.py:116`.** A `news:` item in the case's facts or the release with `date: null` crashes with `TypeError: fromisoformat` in both `compile_evidence` and `signals` (ran). Likewise **`scorecard.py:50-53`**: an `sc` row with `ppm` or `otd_pct` null raises `TypeError` (ran).
   - FIXABLE: skip a row that is missing the field you read.

## Wrong results with no error

3. **`economics.py:43` and `:51`.** `_grid` builds the default plan with `closing_terms(case, {})`, without `standard`. Two effects:
   - A negotiable field with no options keeps the buyer's plan even after you recompile with the supplier's standard terms. I ran: with no `payment_days` options and standard 30, `best_package` gives 60. The API says such a field takes the supplier's standard value, so this sheet may not be valid.
   - For `incoterm`, the kit's default plan is the most expensive term. I ran: P01 with `incoterm` negotiable and no options gives EXW in `best_package`, even with standard `DAP` passed. We would ask for the worst freight.
   - FIXABLE: use `kit.closing_terms(case, {}, standard)`. For `incoterm`, take the keys of `freight_eur_per_unit` as the options.

4. **`forecast_cost_news.py:76` and `signals.py:117`.** News and notes later than the case's letter are dropped. The Sunday release brings market news and letters from early October; a hidden case whose letter is from the package (September) never cites them. I ran: news `2026-10-05` with topic `free_capacity` on P01 gives no claim and an empty signal.
   - FIXABLE: set the upper limit to the case date ("now"), not the letter date.

5. **`signals.py:59-66`.** `_documents` queries only the SQLite `documents` table. The release's documents live in its CSV files, outside the SQLite (`arena_kit/data.py:70`).
   - I ran: a release document stating "price changes above 1 % need the approval…" can be read with `data.document(...)`, yet `committee_above_pct` stays None and `free_capacity` stays empty. The Sunday letters and memo never reach the planner.
   - The CSV layout of my fake release is a guess; the gap is in the code either way.
   - FIXABLE: also go through the release's `doc:` facts and documents rows by supplier.

## Claims the arena could mark wrong, or that help the supplier

6. **`quote.py:14` and `:31`.** The price at stake is the asked price, not the current one. I ran: P01 with a rival quote at 135.00 (current 126.53, asked 138.55) gets cited. That reveals a fallback 6.7 % above today's price and anchors the supplier there. The check is also on unit price only; tooling, lead time and ppm are ignored, so a quote whose total cost is worse can still be cited.
   - FIXABLE: compare with `min(current, asked)`, or with the total cost of the quote's terms against the total cost at the current price.

7. **`quote.py:31`, `forecast_cost_news.py:33`, `economics.py:117-122`.** A part's own figures are compared raw with the case price.
   - Different price units: I ran: on P14 (per 100 pieces), a hidden quote per 1 piece at 3.10 is cited as "a quote for the same part at 3.10 EUR". The figure checks out, but the argument is wrong; and a quote per 100 on a per-piece case would wrongly be skipped.
   - Bundles: P07 mixes parts priced per 100 and per 1,000 under one bundle `unit_price`, so one part's quote or should-cost against the bundle price is meaningless.
   - The package uses one price unit per part, so the risk comes from case facts and bundles.
   - INVESTIGATE: normalise using `parts.price_unit`, and turn off the quote and should-cost comparison for bundles.

8. **`forecast_cost_news.py:48-65`.** Forecast growth is cited in every case type, including capacity cases (P09: +13.2 %, P10: +10.1 %). Telling a supplier with no free capacity that we need more volume strengthens its hand on allocation and price.
   - FIXABLE: skip the forecast when the case `type` is `capacity` or when the `full_order_book` signal is set.

9. **`index.py:91`.** The "is the increase justified" test is a strict `>=` with no margin. P17 has a weighted move of 7.95 % against 8.0 % asked; the code therefore cites labour +2.7 % against an increase that is in fact justified. Series without a value 12 months back drop out of the weighted sum, which pushes it further down.
   - FIXABLE: add a margin, e.g. stay silent when weighted ≥ asked − 1 pt, or when a heavily weighted driver is missing.

10. **The `Claim` contract and `compile.py`.** In RFQs the list holds `sc:` and `news:` claims about different suppliers, and `news:` IDs do not name the supplier, so the planner must look each one up in the facts. A rival quote may be cited to every other bidder, but `quote.py:28` excludes quotes from all case suppliers. That opportunity is lost.
    - INVESTIGATE: this is the routing limit already noted in NOTES.md, with the planner as owner.

## Cost function and caching

11. **`economics.py:86-87` (decision D1).** `Economics.cost` never includes the relationship cost. The arena does charge it: the P01 breakdown has a `relationship` line, and it is 0 there only because that deal was 135.40, above the current price. The only evidence for D1 is that one deal, where the supplier was not squeezed.
    - In stabilise and secure_supply cases (8 of 19), when the planner pushes below the supplier's sustainable margin, `cost`, `best_package` and the levers underestimate the arena's total cost, and nothing flags it.
    - INVESTIGATE: at least make the planner add `relationship_risk` in these cases.

12. **`economics.py:34-38`.** `_c_alt` returns inf whenever `kind == "none"`, while the kit's `closing_move` (`arena_kit/play.py:130`) costs any alternative that has a `unit_price`, whatever its kind. That is a small divergence.

- **Ce que les familles citent sur les 19 cas** :
  - `scorecard` : P05, P06, P09, P11 (2 376 ppm) et P12.
  - `orders` : P14 et P19.
  - `forecast_cost_news` : le should-cost sur P06 et P10, une hausse de nos prévisions sur 15 cas, une news de capacité libre sur P05.
  - `quote` : rien, car chaque devis alternatif est plus cher que le prix en jeu.
- **`signals`** : P02 hausse justifiée, P08 et P14 matière achetée à terme jusqu'en mars 2027, P11 besoin de trésorerie, comité de prix au-delà de 2 % chez 8 fournisseurs. P17 est à la limite : +7,95 % pondéré contre 8 % demandés.

**CRITIQUES (reproduits)**
- [CRITICAL] (9/10) `economics.py:63-68,95-99` : `compile_case` lève `ValueError` et arrête tout le cas quand un cas caché a un must-have :
  - sur le prix (`unit_price <= 130`), parce que le prix est figé au prix demandé pendant la recherche ;
  - ou sur un champ que seul le devis remplit (`ppm_commitment <= 1000` avant le tour 0).
  
  Correctif proposé : ignorer ces must-haves pendant la recherche de la grille, et journaliser au lieu de lever une erreur.

- (8/10) **Release du dimanche invisible** (`signals.py:59`, `forecast_cost_news.py:76`, `orders.py`) :
  - les documents et commandes de la release ne sont pas dans la base SQLite, seule source lue ;

"""compile_evidence(case, data) -> list[Claim]: every verified argument of a case, strongest first.
Facts come from the package, the Sunday release (DataPackage merges `release-sunday` when it is
present) and the hidden case's own `facts`. Every claim is checked before it is returned.
"""
from hollerau.contracts import Claim
from .facts import check, facts_of
from .forecast_cost_news import forecast_cost_news_claims
from .index import index_claims
from .notice import notice_claims
from .orders import orders_claims
from .quote import quote_claims
from .scorecard import scorecard_claims
# order = strength: a contract breach, then a cheaper rival quote, the supplier's own record, cost and index
# data, our order history, then our forecast and the news
FAMILIES = [notice_claims, quote_claims, scorecard_claims, index_claims, orders_claims, forecast_cost_news_claims]
def compile_evidence(case: dict, data) -> list[Claim]:
    facts = facts_of(case, data)
    out, seen = [], set()
    for family in FAMILIES:
        for claim in family(case, data, facts):
            if not check(claim, facts) or seen & set(claim.ids):  # each ID counts once per case
                continue
            seen |= set(claim.ids)
            out.append(claim)
    return out
"""Quote family: a quote of this case (in its `refs` or our alternative) priced below what is at stake.
The arena checks the quote's price, same part (brief/api.md). A rival quote above the price at stake
argues the supplier's case: it is never cited. Citing a rival quote reveals it to the supplier.
"""
from hollerau.contracts import Claim
from .facts import asked_price
def stake_price(case: dict, facts: dict) -> float | None:
    """The price at stake: the letter's asked price, else the current price."""
    return asked_price(case, facts) or case["buyer"].get("current_unit_price")
def case_quotes(case: dict) -> list[str]:
    alt = (case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}).get("ref") or ""
    refs = [r for r in case.get("refs", []) if r.startswith("quote:")] + ([alt] if alt.startswith("quote:") else [])
    return list(dict.fromkeys(refs))
def quote_claims(case: dict, data, facts: dict) -> list[Claim]:
    stake = stake_price(case, facts)
    if stake is None:
        return []
    found = [(q, facts[q]) for q in case_quotes(case) if q in facts]
    found = [(q, f) for q, f in found if f.get("part") in case["parts"] and f.get("supplier") not in case["suppliers"]]
    claims = []
    for q, f in sorted(found, key=lambda qf: qf[1]["unit_price"]):
        if f["unit_price"] >= stake:
            continue
        per = f" per {f['price_unit']} pcs" if (f.get("price_unit") or 1) > 1 else ""
        claims.append(
            Claim(
                family="quote",
                ids=[q],
                figure=f["unit_price"],
                unit="EUR",
                sentence=f"We hold a quote for the same part at {f['unit_price']:.2f} EUR{per} ({q}).",
                supports="price",
            )

    return claims

The arena checks the mean on-time delivery of the cited rows, or their mean ppm if we speak of quality
(brief/api.md). Each `sc` row is already a rolling 12-month figure (P11 letter), so one row is one argument.
OTD is low across the package (KNOWN_ISSUES 1: it depends on the reference date): only a red or amber card
and a clear gap are cited.
"""
from hollerau.contracts import Claim
PPM_LIMIT = 1000  # above this, the quality argument
OTD_LIMIT = 80.0  # below this %, the delivery argument
QUALITY_TYPES = {"quality"}

    """The supplier's scorecard IDs, latest first."""
    prefix = "sc:" + supplier.split(":", 1)[1] + "@"

def _claim(sc_id: str, row: dict, quality: bool) -> Claim:
    quarter = sc_id.rsplit("@", 1)[1]
    if quality:
        return Claim(
            family="scorecard",
            ids=[sc_id],
            figure=float(row["ppm"]),
            unit="ppm",
            sentence=f"Your rolling quality to {quarter} stands at {row['ppm']} ppm ({sc_id}).",
            supports="quality",
        )
    return Claim(
        family="scorecard",
        ids=[sc_id],
        figure=row["otd_pct"],
        unit="%",
        sentence=f"Your rolling on-time delivery to {quarter} stands at {row['otd_pct']:.1f}% ({sc_id}).",
        supports="other",

"""signals(case, data) -> dict: what the planner should know about the supplier, never sent as a claim.

Meeting notes, letters and e-mails are context, not checks (brief/api.md); our late payments are not citable
at all (no `inv:` in facts.json). The package's notes follow fixed wordings, so plain phrase matching is
reliable. Every signal lists the IDs it comes from, so the planner can quote the context in prose.

  asked_pct, asked_price      the letter's demand (None without a price letter)
  weighted_index_pct          per part, the 12-month move of its cost drivers weighted by `cost_drivers`
  increase_justified          the weighted move meets the demand (P02): argue terms, not the price
  suppliers[sup]              per supplier:
    committee_above_pct       price changes above this % need its pricing committee
    material_hedged_until     "Month YYYY" its material or energy is bought forward to (P08, P14)
    cash_need, free_capacity, full_order_book, open_book, reference_customer, small_account_review,
    not_strategic, expects_partnership, list_price_only, overdue_complaints   -> list of IDs
    credit_index_change       supplier_intel credit index now minus 12 months ago (higher = worse)
    single_source             no other active or qualified source for a part of the case
    our_late_payments         {invoices, late_share, avg_days_late} over the 12 months before the case
"""

import re
from datetime import date, timedelta

from .facts import asked_price, facts_of
from .index import asked_pct, driver_moves, weighted_move_pct

NOTE_DAYS = 548  # notes of the last 18 months
PAY_DAYS = 365

PHRASES = {
    "cash_need": ["pay earlier", "pay our invoices within", "spoke mostly about cash"],
    "free_capacity": ["could take additional parts at short notice"],
    "full_order_book": ["order intake is very strong", "very high capacity utilisation"],
    "open_book": ["walk us through their calculation"],
    "reference_customer": ["important reference customer"],
    "small_account_review": ["reviewing small accounts"],
    "not_strategic": ["'not strategic'"],
    "expects_partnership": ["expects partnership"],
    "list_price_only": ["are not discounted", "applies to all customers", "will not be extended"],
    "overdue_complaints": ["invoices are overdue"],
}
NEWS = {
    "free_capacity": "free_capacity",
    "new_plant": "free_capacity",
    "full_order_book": "full_order_book",
    "allocation": "full_order_book",
    "credit_downgrade": "cash_need",
    "credit_watch": "cash_need",
    "short_time_work": "cash_need",
}
COMMITTEE = re.compile(r"price changes above ([\d.]+) ?% need the approval")
HEDGED = re.compile(r"(?:forward|at fixed prices) until (\w+ \d{4})")


def reference_date(case: dict, facts: dict) -> date | None:
    doc = facts.get(case.get("trigger_doc") or "") or {}
    return date.fromisoformat(doc["date"]) if doc.get("date") else None


def _documents(data, supplier: str, since: date | None, until: date | None) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    rows = data.query("SELECT id, date FROM documents WHERE supplier_id = ? ORDER BY date", (supplier,), limit=1000)
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        d = date.fromisoformat(r["date"])
        if (since and d < since) or (until and d > until):
            continue
        out.append((r["id"], " ".join(data.document(r["id"]).split())))
    return out


def _late_payments(data, supplier: str, until: date | None) -> dict:
    end = until or date.max
    start = end - timedelta(days=PAY_DAYS) if until else date.min
    rows = data.query(
        "SELECT due_date, paid_date FROM invoices WHERE supplier_id = ? AND paid_date IS NOT NULL",
        (supplier,),
        limit=100_000,
    )
    rows = [r for r in rows if start <= date.fromisoformat(r["due_date"]) <= end]
    late = [(date.fromisoformat(r["paid_date"]) - date.fromisoformat(r["due_date"])).days for r in rows]
    late = [d for d in late if d > 0]
    return {
        "invoices": len(rows),
        "late_share": round(len(late) / len(rows), 3) if rows else 0.0,
        "avg_days_late": round(sum(late) / len(late), 1) if late else 0.0,
    }


def _single_source(data, case: dict, supplier: str) -> bool:
    for part in case["parts"]:
        rows = data.query("SELECT supplier_id, status FROM sourcing WHERE part_id = ?", (part,))
        others = [r for r in rows if r["supplier_id"] != supplier and r["status"] in ("active", "qualified")]
        if not others:
            return True
    return False


def supplier_signals(case: dict, data, facts: dict, supplier: str) -> dict:
    ref = reference_date(case, facts)
    since = ref - timedelta(days=NOTE_DAYS) if ref else None
    out: dict = {name: [] for name in PHRASES}
    out["committee_above_pct"] = out["material_hedged_until"] = None
    for doc_id, text in _documents(data, supplier, since, ref):
        low = text.lower()
        for name, phrases in PHRASES.items():
            if any(p in low for p in phrases):
                out[name].append(doc_id)
        if m := COMMITTEE.search(low):
            out["committee_above_pct"] = float(m.group(1))
            out.setdefault("committee", []).append(doc_id)
        if m := HEDGED.search(text):
            out["material_hedged_until"] = m.group(1)
            out.setdefault("material_hedged", []).append(doc_id)
    for nid, n in sorted(facts.items()):
        if not nid.startswith("news:") or n.get("supplier") != supplier or n.get("topic") not in NEWS:
            continue
        d = date.fromisoformat(n["date"])
        if (since and d < since) or (ref and d > ref):
            continue
        out[NEWS[n["topic"]]].append(nid)
    intel = data.query(
        "SELECT credit_index, credit_index_12m_ago FROM supplier_intel WHERE supplier_id = ?", (supplier,)
    )
    out["credit_index_change"] = (
        intel[0]["credit_index"] - intel[0]["credit_index_12m_ago"]
        if intel and intel[0]["credit_index"] is not None and intel[0]["credit_index_12m_ago"] is not None
        else None
    )
    out["single_source"] = _single_source(data, case, supplier)
    out["our_late_payments"] = _late_payments(data, supplier, ref)
    return out


def signals(case: dict, data) -> dict:
    facts = facts_of(case, data)
    asked = asked_pct(case, facts)
    weighted = {}
    for part in case["parts"]:
        moves = driver_moves(part, data, facts)
        if moves:
            weighted[part] = round(weighted_move_pct(moves), 2)
    return {
        "asked_pct": asked,
        "asked_price": asked_price(case, facts),
        "weighted_index_pct": weighted,
        "increase_justified": None if asked is None or not weighted else any(w >= asked for w in weighted.values()),
        "suppliers": {s: supplier_signals(case, data, facts, s) for s in case["suppliers"]},
    }

import copy
import json
import logging
import math
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from arena_kit.data import DataPackage
from hollerau.evidence import facts as facts_mod
from hollerau.evidence.compile import compile_evidence
from hollerau.evidence.economics import compile_case, estimate_supplier
from hollerau.evidence.facts import check, facts_of, load_package
from hollerau.evidence.forecast_cost_news import forecast_cost_news_claims
from hollerau.evidence.quote import quote_claims
from hollerau.evidence.signals import signals

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
CASES = {c["case_id"]: c for c in json.loads((ROOT / "tests/fixtures/cases/practice.json").read_text())}


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def data():
    try:
        return load_package()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pytest.skip("no data package: run `uv run arena data` or set ARENA_DATA")


def ids_of(claims, prefix):
    return [c.ids[0] for c in claims if c.ids[0].startswith(prefix)]


# 1. Golden rule: never raise


CORRUPT_FACTS = {
    "doc:20260911-70110-P01": "not a dict",
    "news:BAD-1": {"supplier": "sup:70110", "topic": "free_capacity", "date": None, "headline": None},
    "news:BAD-2": {"supplier": "sup:70110", "topic": "free_capacity", "date": "yesterday", "headline": "x"},
    "sc:70110@2026Q4": {"supplier": "sup:70110", "ppm": None, "otd_pct": "n/a", "colour": "red"},
    "quote:7200001": {"part": "part:310010", "supplier": "sup:70140", "unit_price": "cheap"},
    "fc:310010@2026-12": {"part": "part:310010", "change_pct": None},
    "cost:310010": {"part": "part:310010", "unit_cost": None},
    "idx:PPI-D351@2026-09": {"series": "PPI-D351", "value": None},
    "ctr:4600070110": {"supplier": "sup:70110", "days": None},
}


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "corrupt",
    [
        lambda c: c.update(facts=CORRUPT_FACTS),
        lambda c: c["buyer"].pop("freight_eur_per_unit"),
        lambda c: c.update(negotiable=["unit_price", "no_such_field"], term_options={"no_such_field": [None, 3]}),
        lambda c: c.update(parts=None, suppliers=None),
        lambda c: c.update(buyer=None),
        lambda c: c.clear(),
    ],
)
def test_corrupt_case_never_raises(data, corrupt):
    case = copy.deepcopy(CASES["case:P01"])
    corrupt(case)
    econ = compile_case(case, data=data)
    assert isinstance(econ.levers, list) and isinstance(econ.best_package, dict)
    assert isinstance(econ.cost({"unit_price": 130.0}), float)
    assert isinstance(econ.must_haves_ok({"unit_price": 130.0}), bool)
    claims = compile_evidence(case, data)
    assert all(check(c, facts_of(case, data)) for c in claims)
    assert isinstance(signals(case, data), dict)


def test_corrupt_facts_keep_the_good_claims(data):
    """A family that meets broken facts drops them; the notice and index claims of P01 stay."""
    case = copy.deepcopy(CASES["case:P01"])
    case["facts"] = {k: v for k, v in CORRUPT_FACTS.items() if not k.startswith(("doc:", "ctr:"))}
    families = {c.family for c in compile_evidence(case, data)}
    assert {"notice", "index"} <= families

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "must_have",
    [
        {"field": "unit_price", "op": "<=", "value": 130},  # the price is the planner's call
        {"field": "ppm_commitment", "op": "<=", "value": 1000},  # only the supplier's quote fills it (round 0)
    ],
)
def test_untestable_must_have_is_left_out_of_the_search(data, caplog, must_have):
    case = copy.deepcopy(CASES["case:P01"])
    case["buyer"]["must_haves"] = [must_have]
    with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING):
        econ = compile_case(case, data=data)
    assert f"must-have on {must_have['field']} left out" in caplog.text
    assert econ.best_package == compile_case(CASES["case:P01"], data=data).best_package
    assert [lv.field for lv in econ.levers] == ["effective_date", "payment_days"]


def test_quote_field_must_have_is_tested_once_the_standard_is_known(data):
    case = copy.deepcopy(CASES["case:P01"])
    case["buyer"]["must_haves"] = [{"field": "ppm_commitment", "op": "<=", "value": 1000}]
    econ = compile_case(case, {"ppm_commitment": 900}, data=data)

    assert not compile_case(case, {"ppm_commitment": 1200}, data=data).must_haves_ok({"unit_price": 130.0})

def test_null_rows_are_skipped(data):
    case = copy.deepcopy(CASES["case:P11"])
    case["facts"] = {
        "sc:70140@2026Q4": {"supplier": "sup:70140", "ppm": None, "otd_pct": None, "colour": "red"},
        "news:NULL-1": {"supplier": "sup:70140", "topic": "free_capacity", "date": None, "headline": "x"},

def release_data(data, tmp_path):

    (tmp_path / "data").mkdir()

                                 "supplier": "sup:70110", "topic": "free_capacity"}}
    letter = {"doc:20261006-70110-S1": {"date": "2026-10-06", "supplier": "sup:70110", "type": "letter"}}

    (tmp_path / "correspondence" / "20261006-70110-S1.md").write_text(
        "# Annual review\n\nletter - 2026-10-06 - Brandlhuber\n\n"
        "Their key account manager explained that price changes above 1 % need the approval of their pricing "
        "committee, which meets every two weeks.\n"
    )
    (tmp_path / "data" / "documents.csv").write_text(
        "id,date,kind,supplier_id,part_ids,subject,author,file\n"
        "doc:20261006-70110-S1,2026-10-06,letter,sup:70110,,Annual review,,correspondence/20261006-70110-S1.md\n"
    )
    return DataPackage(data.root, release=tmp_path)


def test_release_news_reaches_claims_and_signals(release_data):

    assert "news:20261005-90" in ids_of(compile_evidence(case, release_data), "news:")
    s = signals(case, release_data)["suppliers"]["sup:70110"]
    assert "news:20261005-90" in s["free_capacity"]


def test_release_letters_reach_signals(release_data):
    s = signals(CASES["case:P01"], release_data)["suppliers"]["sup:70110"]
    assert s["committee_above_pct"] == 1.0 and "doc:20261006-70110-S1" in s["committee"]


def test_news_after_the_case_start_is_not_used(release_data):
    case = copy.deepcopy(CASES["case:P01"])
    case["start_date"] = "2026-10-01"
    assert "news:20261005-90" not in ids_of(compile_evidence(case, release_data), "news:")


# 5. No cached failure


def test_a_failed_load_is_not_cached(data, monkeypatch):
    calls = []

    def flaky():
        calls.append(1)
        if len(calls) == 1:
            raise FileNotFoundError("not downloaded yet")
        return data

    monkeypatch.setattr(facts_mod, "load_package", flaky)
    monkeypatch.setattr(facts_mod, "_loaded", None)
    assert facts_of(CASES["case:P01"]) == {}  # first call: no package yet
    assert compile_case(CASES["case:P01"]).reference_price == 138.55  # second call loads it: D3 works
    assert len(calls) == 2


# 6. Forecast growth never told to a saturated supplier


@pytest.mark.parametrize("case_id", ["case:P09", "case:P10"])
def test_no_forecast_claim_in_capacity_cases(data, case_id):
    case = CASES[case_id]
    assert ids_of(forecast_cost_news_claims(case, data, facts_of(case, data)), "fc:") == []


def test_no_forecast_claim_to_a_supplier_that_allocates(data):
    case = copy.deepcopy(CASES["case:P01"])
    assert ids_of(forecast_cost_news_claims(case, data, facts_of(case, data)), "fc:")  # growth cited normally
    case["facts"] = {"news:ALLOC-1": {"date": "2026-09-01", "headline": "Brandlhuber allocates",
                                      "supplier": "sup:70110", "topic": "allocation"}}
    assert ids_of(forecast_cost_news_claims(case, data, facts_of(case, data)), "fc:") == []


# 7. Index: an increase within 1 point of the weighted move is justified


def test_p17_increase_within_a_point_is_justified(data):
    case = CASES["case:P17"]  # weighted +7.95 % against +8.0 % asked
    assert [c for c in compile_evidence(case, data) if c.family == "index"] == []
    assert signals(case, data)["increase_justified"] is True


# 8. Quotes and should-cost only when comparable with the case price


def test_quote_in_another_price_unit_is_not_cited(data):
    case = copy.deepcopy(CASES["case:P14"])  # motor cable, priced per 100
    case["refs"].append("quote:HIDDEN-PU")
    case["facts"] = {"quote:HIDDEN-PU": {"part": "part:350040", "supplier": "sup:70999", "unit_price": 3.10,
                                         "price_unit": 1}}
    assert quote_claims(case, data, facts_of(case, data)) == []
    case["facts"]["quote:HIDDEN-PU"] |= {"unit_price": 300.0, "price_unit": 100}
    assert ids_of(quote_claims(case, data, facts_of(case, data)), "quote:") == ["quote:HIDDEN-PU"]


def test_no_quote_or_should_cost_in_a_bundle(data):
    case = copy.deepcopy(CASES["case:P07"])  # a kit of four parts, one price
    case["refs"].append("quote:HIDDEN-KIT")
    case["facts"] = {
        "quote:HIDDEN-KIT": {"part": "part:360010", "supplier": "sup:70999", "unit_price": 1.0, "price_unit": 100},
        "cost:360010": {"part": "part:360010", "unit_cost": 1.0, "price_unit": 100},
    }
    facts = facts_of(case, data)
    assert quote_claims(case, data, facts) == []
    assert ids_of(forecast_cost_news_claims(case, data, facts), "cost:") == []
    assert estimate_supplier(case, data=data)["estimated"]


def test_should_cost_in_another_price_unit_is_not_used(data):
    case = copy.deepcopy(CASES["case:P14"])
    case["facts"] = {"cost:350040": {"part": "part:350040", "unit_cost": 2.0, "price_unit": 1}}
    facts = facts_of(case, data)
    assert ids_of(forecast_cost_news_claims(case, data, facts), "cost:") == []
    supplier = estimate_supplier(case, data=data)
    assert supplier["estimated"] and not math.isclose(supplier["full_cost"], 2.0)

import copy
import json
import logging
import math
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from arena_kit.data import DataPackage
from hollerau.evidence import facts as facts_mod

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
CASES = {c["case_id"]: c for c in json.loads((ROOT / "tests/fixtures/cases/practice.json").read_text())}


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def data():
    try:
        return load_package()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pytest.skip("no data package: run `uv run arena data` or set ARENA_DATA")


def ids_of(claims, prefix):
    return [c.ids[0] for c in claims if c.ids[0].startswith(prefix)]


# 1. Golden rule: never raise


CORRUPT_FACTS = {
    "doc:20260911-70110-P01": "not a dict",
    "news:BAD-1": {"supplier": "sup:70110", "topic": "free_capacity", "date": None, "headline": None},
    "news:BAD-2": {"supplier": "sup:70110", "topic": "free_capacity", "date": "yesterday", "headline": "x"},
    "sc:70110@2026Q4": {"supplier": "sup:70110", "ppm": None, "otd_pct": "n/a", "colour": "red"},
    "quote:7200001": {"part": "part:310010", "supplier": "sup:70140", "unit_price": "cheap"},
    "fc:310010@2026-12": {"part": "part:310010", "change_pct": None},
    "cost:310010": {"part": "part:310010", "unit_cost": None},
    "idx:PPI-D351@2026-09": {"series": "PPI-D351", "value": None},
    "ctr:4600070110": {"supplier": "sup:70110", "days": None},
}


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "corrupt",
    [
        lambda c: c.update(facts=CORRUPT_FACTS),
        lambda c: c["buyer"].pop("freight_eur_per_unit"),
        lambda c: c.update(negotiable=["unit_price", "no_such_field"], term_options={"no_such_field": [None, 3]}),
        lambda c: c.update(parts=None, suppliers=None),
        lambda c: c.update(buyer=None),
        lambda c: c.clear(),
    ],
)
def test_corrupt_case_never_raises(data, corrupt):
    case = copy.deepcopy(CASES["case:P01"])
    corrupt(case)
    econ = compile_case(case, data=data)
    assert isinstance(econ.levers, list) and isinstance(econ.best_package, dict)
    assert isinstance(econ.cost({"unit_price": 130.0}), float)
    assert isinstance(econ.must_haves_ok({"unit_price": 130.0}), bool)
    claims = compile_evidence(case, data)
    assert all(check(c, facts_of(case, data)) for c in claims)
    assert isinstance(signals(case, data), dict)

    case = copy.deepcopy(CASES["case:P01"])

    families = {c.family for c in compile_evidence(case, data)}
    assert {"notice", "index"} <= families

@pytest.mark.parametrize(

    ],
)

    assert econ.best_package == compile_case(CASES["case:P01"], data=data).best_package
    assert [lv.field for lv in econ.levers] == ["effective_date", "payment_days"]

    assert not compile_case(case, {"ppm_commitment": 1200}, data=data).must_haves_ok({"unit_price": 130.0})

Chaque correctif a son test dans `tests/test_hardening.py`. Contrôle par mutation : en réintroduisant l'ancien comportement (index, forecast, release), les tests concernés échouent.

1. **Règle d'or : jamais d'exception.** `compile_case`, `compile_evidence` et `signals` attrapent les erreurs par étape, par famille et par fournisseur. Ils journalisent (`log.exception`) et rendent un résultat vide : pas de leviers, `best_package` vide, `c_alt` infini, aucun claim pour la famille en échec, signaux à leur valeur vide. `Economics.cost` renvoie l'infini et `must_haves_ok` renvoie `False` en cas d'erreur. Test : 6 cas corrompus (faits absurdes, `buyer` absent, cas vide…).
2. **Must-haves que la grille ne peut pas tester.** Un must-have sur le prix (décision du planificateur), ou sur un champ que seul le devis remplit tant que le standard n'est pas lu, est écarté de la recherche, avec un warning. `Economics.must_haves_ok` garde tous les must-haves. 3. **Valeurs nulles** : toute ligne de faits avec un champ nul ou absent est ignorée (`has()`). `check()` renvoie `False` au lieu de planter.
4. **Release du dimanche.** Les documents (`data/documents.csv` de la release) et les commandes (`data/po_lines.csv`, si présent) sont lus en plus de la SQLite ; les news arrivent par `facts`. 6. **Forecast** : aucun claim « hausse de nos volumes » dans un cas `capacity`, ni pour un fournisseur dont le carnet est plein ou qui alloue (notes, lettres, news : `saturated()`). P09 et P10 n'en ont plus.
7. **Index** : la hausse est justifiée si la variation pondérée atteint la demande à 1 point près. P17 (+7,95 % contre 8 %) n'a plus de claim index, et `increase_justified` y est vrai.
8. **Quote et should-cost** : on les compare au plus bas entre prix courant et prix demandé. Ni l'un ni l'autre n'est cité ni utilisé dans `estimate_supplier` si son `price_unit` diffère de celui de la pièce, ou si le cas est un kit (`bundling` ou plusieurs pièces).

- `_grid` ignore le standard du devis pour un champ négociable **sans** options : l'incoterm partirait du plus cher.
- Les factures impayées échues ne comptent pas dans `our_late_payments`.

La décision ne repose que sur le deal P01, conclu au-dessus du prix courant. Proposition : le planificateur ajoute `relationship_risk(case, terms, standard, data=data)` dans ces cas, ou on calibre `full_cost` sur des sessions validées.
- **`Claim` n'a pas de champ fournisseur.** Dans un appel d'offres à plusieurs fournisseurs (P05, P06), les claims `sc:` et `news:` concernent chacun un fournisseur précis : le planificateur doit les router d'après l'ID (`sc:<n°>@…`, `facts[news]["supplier"]`). Envoyé au mauvais fournisseur, un claim est `irrelevant`. Une modification du contrat (`Claim.supplier_id`) passe par `Décisions.md`.
- **`c_alt` pour une alternative `kind: none`.** Ici, c'est l'infini dès que `kind == "none"`. Le kit (`arena_kit/play.py:130`, `closing_move`) coûte toute alternative qui a un `unit_price`, quel que soit son type. Aucun des 19 cas n'est concerné (une alternative `none` n'a jamais de prix). Laquelle des deux règles suit l'arène ?

""" + s[i:]
rep("1. Revue `/review` (rapport seulement) : voir le rapport de la session du 10/10 soir.\n",
    "1. Revue `/review` (rapport seulement) faite le 10/10 soir, puis correctifs 1 à 8 ci-dessus.\n")
p.write_text(s)
EOF

  - capacité libre ou carnet plein, source unique, nos retards de paiement.

Une modification du contrat (`Claim.supplier_id`) passe par `Décisions.md`.

- un champ négociable sans options ignore le standard du devis (l'incoterm partirait du plus cher) ;
- les factures impayées échues ne comptent pas dans nos retards de paiement.

input.command:
gh pr create --base main --head nevil/evidence --title "Economics lane: compile_case + compile_evidence + signals" --body-file - <<'EOF'
> **Ne pas merger sans revue.** Icham décide du merge.

## Ce qui est fait (`hollerau/evidence/`, rien d'autre)

- `compile_case(case, standard=None, data=None) -> Economics` (`economics.py`) : coût C de toute term sheet (fonction de coût du kit, conditions standard du devis appliquées), meilleur paquet hors prix sous must-haves, leviers triés par coût d'oubli, `c_alt`, prix de référence. En plus : `estimate_supplier`, `relationship_risk`.
- `compile_evidence(case, data) -> list[Claim]` (`compile.py`) : six familles, chacune revérifiée comme le fait l'arène (`facts.check`), chaque ID une seule fois par cas. Elles sont classées de la plus forte à la plus faible : `notice`, `quote`, `scorecard`, `index`, `orders`, `forecast_cost_news`.
- `signals(case, data) -> dict` (`signals.py`) : contexte pour le planificateur, jamais envoyé comme claim. On y trouve :
  - hausse justifiée, matière couverte jusqu'à une date, besoin de trésorerie, comité de prix ;
  - capacité libre ou carnet plein, source unique, nos retards de paiement.
- Règle d'or : aucune de ces trois fonctions ne lève d'exception. Une étape ou une famille en échec est journalisée et rend un résultat vide.
- Lit la release du dimanche (documents, commandes, news) jusqu'au début du cas.
- 140 tests (`hollerau/evidence/tests/`), ruff check et ruff format propres. Tout tourne hors ligne : aucune session arena.

En finale, **passer `data` explicitement** (package + release du dimanche) à `compile_case`, `compile_evidence` et `signals`.

## Contrôle croisé avec l'arène (session P01 enregistrée)

`cost` des termes négociables du deal P01, complétés par les conditions standard du fournisseur, est égal à `c_deal` = **1 120 579,36 €** de l'arène, à 0,01 € près. `c_alt` = 1 176 178,02 € est identique lui aussi (`tests/fixtures/sessions/P01-naive.json`).

Le PDF du devis n'est pas dans la fixture. Le standard du test est donc reconstruit à partir des champs du deal ni négociables ni fixés (ppm 900, chargeback 0). Avec ce standard, le poste qualité vaut exactement les 1 584,36 € de l'arène.

## Décisions

- **D1, `cost` sans coût de relation.** `Economics.cost` = `arena_kit.cost.total_cost(case, terms, standard)`, sans estimation du fournisseur. Avec le should-cost comme coût complet, le deal P01 aurait coûté 4 055 € de relation, alors que l'arène facture 0. L'estimation est exposée à part, dans `relationship_risk()`.
- **D2, valeurs permises = `term_options` seulement.** Un champ négociable sans options garde le plan acheteur, n'est pas un levier, et émet un warning.
- **D3, leviers évalués au prix demandé** (`asked_price` de la lettre, sinon le prix courant). Sur P01, `effective_date` vaut 16 263 € (2027-01-01) et 40 257 € (2027-04-01) par rapport à 2026-11-01. C'est le levier n°1. À reporter dans `Décisions.md`.
- **Unités de prix.** Les prix des cas sont exprimés dans le `price_unit` de la pièce, comme les données (P14 : pour 100 pièces). On compare donc sans diviser. Un devis ou un should-cost dans une autre unité, ou dans un cas « kit », n'est ni cité ni utilisé.

## À voir avec Icham

- **D1, `cost` sans le coût de relation.** Dans les 8 cas `stabilise` / `secure_supply`, si le planificateur pousse le fournisseur sous sa marge soutenable, l'arène facture un poste `relationship` que `Economics.cost` ignore. `cost`, `best_package` et les leviers sous-estiment alors C. La décision ne repose que sur le deal P01, conclu au-dessus du prix courant. Proposition : le planificateur ajoute `relationship_risk(case, terms, standard, data=data)` dans ces cas, ou on calibre `full_cost` sur des sessions validées.
- **`Claim` n'a pas de champ fournisseur.** Dans un appel d'offres à plusieurs fournisseurs (P05, P06), les claims `sc:` et `news:` concernent chacun un fournisseur précis. Le planificateur doit les router d'après l'ID (`sc:<n°>@…`, `facts[news]["supplier"]`). Envoyé au mauvais fournisseur, un claim est `irrelevant`. Une modification du contrat (`Claim.supplier_id`) passe par `Décisions.md`.
- **`c_alt` pour une alternative `kind: none`.** Ici, c'est l'infini dès que `kind == "none"`. Le kit (`arena_kit/play.py:130`, `closing_move`) coûte toute alternative qui a un `unit_price`, quel que soit son type. Aucun des 19 cas n'est concerné. Laquelle des deux règles suit l'arène ?

Restent ouverts, hors du périmètre de cette PR :
- un champ négociable sans options ignore le standard du devis (l'incoterm partirait du plus cher) ;
- les factures impayées échues ne comptent pas dans nos retards de paiement.

Détail complet : `hollerau/evidence/NOTES.md`.

# Décision — titre

Icham

Date : {{date}}
